body.statement: Determine the exact computational complexity of \(\operatorname{CompOpt}(\widetilde W,\mathcal G,\ell;g,r,c)\) for exactly encoded rational \(\widetilde W\in\mathbb Q^{p\times q}\) satisfying the canonical-model promise, both without a prescribed pair and with one prescribed local pair. Resolve one of two branches: either construct a deterministic algorithm \(\mathsf A_{\min}\) that returns an attaining legal completion or an infeasibility certificate in time polynomial in \(p\), \(q\), and the input bit length, or prove an exact hardness classification and identify a nontrivial structurally restricted tractable regime. The resolution must use the elimination, separation-oracle, or rational cancellation-gadget handle in \(\text{def:completion-handle}\), account for coupled downstream cancellations, and correctly recover the optimum and complete minimizer projection of \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{plat}}\).
body.justification: A genuine algorithm-versus-hardness classification is the unresolved step governing whether the exact population image can be computed scalably on the full published class.
body.gap: Yang et al.'s Algorithm 2 has a multiplicative Cartesian choice factor, but enumeration cost proves neither polynomial solvability nor hardness; maximum-flow identification and linear-delay MEC traversal solve different combinatorial objects.
body.consumer: The classification will either supply a scalable exact image routine or delimit the structural regimes in which exact mixed-DOG effect reporting is computationally feasible.

obligation.what_is_open: The exact unrestricted complexity of \(\operatorname{CompOpt}(\widetilde W,\mathcal G,\ell;g,r,c)\), both unconstrained and with a prescribed pair, remains unclassified.
obligation.obstruction: The support counts of \(Q_\omega^{-1}\), \(D_\omega\), and \(B^L_\omega\) contain exact rational cancellations coupled across several groups. The faithful plateau proves that strict coordinate descent and an additive local edge score fail, but it is neither a hardness reduction nor a polynomial-size state representation.
obligation.attempted: The available routes were fraction-free ordered elimination with a rank signature, separation over feasible signatures, scalar dynamic programming, and exact cancellation gadgets. No polynomial bound on the signature space or separation oracle was derived, and no gadget reduction preserving the canonical, minimal, rank-faithful promise was completed.
obligation.partial_result: The exact oracle-to-image reduction is proved in \(\text{thm:projected-oracle-reduction}\), and \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{plat}}\) is an exact faithful witness that neither strict one-group descent nor an additive per-group edge score solves the general problem. A nontrivial polynomial restriction does close: if at most one group \(g_0\) has more than one legal local pair, then \(|\Omega|\le |R_{g_0}||K_{g_0}|\le pq\). Enumerating those pairs, rejecting illegal pivots, evaluating the four reconstruction blocks by fraction-free elimination, and taking the smallest exact support count solves both the unconstrained and prescribed-pair problems. For an input of bit length \(B\), every intermediate determinant has bit length polynomial in \(p+q+B\), so this enumeration is polynomial in the required bit model. What remains open is the unrestricted complexity classification when several groups interact through cancellation in \(Q_\omega^{-1}\), \(D_\omega\), and \(B^L_\omega\).
